tips.comment: Cameletta Vega started her career with a win in a bumper at this meeting last year and returned to the winner's enclosure last time, switching to hurdles at Cork, making all to comfortably win a mares' maiden hurdle 82 days ago. She made one mistake at Cork, but otherwise, she looked a decent hurdler in the making and could cope with the rise in class.

Won impressively on hurdles debut last time, winning with plenty in hand, hardly having come off the bridle. Pleasing to the eye, looking an exciting hurdling prospect and should have a good chance in this.

The model I run suggests Keep Up can win this one. Keep Up lines up here with the second highest RPR of the smaller 10-horse field but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated off this mark. He has shown some form coming into this with figures of 15-1 and needs to show more improvement against stiffer opposition. The jockey on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which helps over the trip. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Looks stable 2nd string here based on jockey bookings, but has won their maiden/novice hurdles last twice in good fashion and does look to be an improving juvenile hurdler. Good jockey back up and top trainer has done well here last 5 seasons, making current 16/1 decent Ew value in the race.
Not a regular winner and has a wider than ideal draw, but this is a weak contest for Listed level. She has a very strong form chance at these weights, with trip and ground no issue.
Placed in 4 listed races last season. Not shown that form so far this season, but looks well in at weights. Can go close if recapturing its best form.

Maiden winner over course and distance in September last year. Highly tried since. Last in the Irish 1,000 Guineas. Behind Fiery Lucy and Shiota last time but it's still early days with these three year old fillies and a return to Galway may suit.

Has looked a winner in waiting since being sent handicapping, shaping as if he is desperate for the step up in trip. His pedigree would suggest that the longer distance is going to be a big plus for him.
Has some good recent form and this drop back in trip ought to help. Has won over farther and if stamina becomes a factor, ought to be involved.
Could be a lively each-way option. Has run over this distance on the flat before and is much better off at the weights this time around. Could go well.

A return to turf could help Enziya, whose connections will be wanting him to improve on his Limerick win, which came before a run at Dundalk last time. He could still be well treated with the possibility of further improvement and a positive jockey booking for the yard.

The model I run suggests Garrick Painter can win this one. Garrick Painter lines up here with the second highest RPR of the larger 18 horse field and is the highest rated official ranking. This leaves him carrying the joint highest weight around this 1m 4f round trip. Drawn in stall 6, so shouldn't pose too many problems from a draw perspective over the longer 1m 4f distance. Comes here after a huge time away and hasn't run for over a year, hence the huge price. But if near good form and race fitness is there, could go close. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Has won just once from 14 starts but has placed on 5 occasions. Will stay this trip and has an each-way chance off what looks like a competitive mark.

Natalia Lupini (SR 25%; winner here this week) trained handicap debutant Dreamed To Dream is bred for staying trips by Arc winner Sottsass out of (Derby winner) Camelot mare. Steps up in trip now and much less exposed than many. Leigh Roche rides.

Paul Townend has chosen the 7-year-old over three other Mullins runners, and that looks like the correct choice to me. I thought he ran as well as could be expected up against seasoned handicappers in the Sussex Champion Chase at Plumpton last April on only his fifth run over fences and got off the mark in pleasing fashion at Ballinrobe last May.

The Gordon Elliott-trained Pied Piper has to concede weight all around, but he is 10 lbs clear on the ratings on a mark of 140. He is by far the best hurdler in this race with a top rating of 157. He won a Grade 2 juvenile hurdle, then finished 3rd in the Triumph Hurdle at the Festival. He is 3 from 3 since taking on the bigger obstacles, and there should be more to come.

Goes up in grade. Off a nice weight. Having her 2nd run at this venue.
She's very lightly raced over fences. Just 3 runs to date. Consistently running well in her short chase career. She managed to get her head in front 2nd time up, beating Anyharminasking comfortably, with just over 6L separating them at the line.
She ran a great race in defeat last time out, especially given the circumstances. She was giving 11lbs in weight to a thriving horse in Hecouldbetheone. She was in the process of running a cracker, looked to have the upper hand when making a terrible blunder at the 3rd last fence. That clearly cost her the race, given she was only beaten just over 1L by the winner at the line.
She won a listed novice hurdle race at this meeting last season, battering the opposition, beating nearest pursuer Le Coq Hardi by 10L. A dominant, easy success. If she runs a similar race here, she would have decent claims off this type of weight.

Good race. The Willie Mullins contingent all command respect. Gold Dancer hadn't shown much form-wise before jumping well to win at Tipperary last time. Not the choice of Paul Townend (Sean O'Keeffe rides) but has claims nonetheless. 6yo by Doctor Dino. Can build on recent win.

Bolted up on his chase debut at Limerick, looking a natural. Had shown solid form on the flat and over hurdles prior to that but he left that form miles behind over the bigger obstacles and can go on to better things.
Special Cadeau is steadily improving, ran a strong second to a fitter rival last time, and the form has been boosted. With fitness now sharpened, he’s primed to strike under O’Keeffe.

Worth an each-way bet, though may need softer ground to be at her best. Relatively lightly raced mare who won her novice on reappearance run in May, and her official mark of 132 probably underestimates her. But even that mark puts her right there on the numbers.
Finished 2nd in this race last year and is probably better this year, having finished runner-up in the County Hurdle at Cheltenham. Should go close.
Has some strong form over obstacles and made a good comeback run last time when landing a good-looking handicap on the flat. If his jumping is sound, he has a good chance.
Has only run once since winning at Leopardstown in December, but that resulted in a 2nd place finish in a Grade 3 race at Tipperary. A repeat of that form gives an each-way chance.

Given Willie Mullins' record in this, 5 out of the last 10 runnings, and the fact Paul Townend has chosen the 6yo mare from a possible 6 runners for the stable, this is too big a price. She's only had 3 runs for the yard, so is unexposed, and this drop back to a stiff 2 miles should suit her, following her good 4th in a competitive handicap at Punchestown's Festival over an extended 2m4f.

The Galway Hurdle is always very competitive and Joseph O'Brien has obviously been playing around with the well backed favourite, but at a decent price Dysart Enos could go well. He has failed to fully deliver what he promised in his early days, but a fast run race in a big field should suit and if he recaptured his Greatwood hurdle form from Cheltenham in November, he should go very well.

The model I run suggests Bowensonfire can win this one. Bowensonfire has a comparably high RPR to the other runners here but has an official ranking that leaves him looking very well treated off this mark. Youngest runner here and has improved a lot in recent runs, form figures of 12-131 and looks to step up again. Not much form on offer for most of the other horses and the weight difference over the 2m trip is quite considerable. 1 and a half stone to top weight. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Lost his form since winning a Grade 2 novice at Fairyhouse. The pick of his form has come right-handed, and all four of his starts since that Grade 2 win have been going the other way. Close second in a handicap hurdle at this meeting last year, and Harry Cobden has four winners and a second on seven rides for Willie Mullins.

Useful hurdler who had a prep run on the flat to hopefully put him spot on for this. Was a creditable fifth to the Harry Derham raider Ascending Lark in a listed handicap at Punchestown on his last hurdling run.
Makes handicap debut off 133, and he has several bits of form where he has run to that sort of mark, including when narrowly beaten around here in October.

Top stable run 5 here, but selection was not far behind a lot of these on comeback run, when coming 4/12 beaten 5.5 lengths in a Grade 3 over 2 miles @ Tipperary. Entitled to come on for that run, good jockey booked and master trainer is tops here numerically last 5 seasons, making current 22/1 worth Ew consideration in the race.

Warttime Leader is a 5-year-old son of Churchill ex Katiyra who won at Group 2 level at 1m2f. Last time out on his racecourse debut in a 4-year-olds only bumper, he finished 1 length second at 9/2 behind Shuttle Diplomacy 100/30f by Dschingis Secret in January '24. That bumper has produced three winners from two runners. He'll now be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins in this 2m2f bumper. I think he can progress here and break his maiden tag. I make him my Nap of the day.

The model I run suggests Garahon can win this one. Garahon lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 17-runner field but has not been penalized for it in the weights. All horses step out carrying the initial same amount of weight around this 2m 2f national hunt flat. Garahon came an improving second on last outing 26 days ago and can build on from that to get over the line first. Headgear applied for the first time to help - tongue tie added for the first time. Unsure if noteworthy or not - but only horse wearing headgear. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Bold Rhyme is not entirely ruled out. Two fair efforts in bumpers so far, both this month. Has stayed on in each of those (by Yeats out of a Supreme Leader mare, so has that ability). Feasible he could progress further on third start. DM Christie trained.

This gelding by Australia is well drawn and could be poised to strike now on his 3rd start for his current stable having been brought in from the all conquering Haggas yard. His third at Yarmouth on debut was behind a future Group winner and ahead of some horses rated around the 90 mark so considering that was his debut, I'd say he could well be up to winning this off 84.

Four times winner over this distance, The David Loughnane trained Bravo Zulu arrives in great form and has won two in a row including a good handicap at Windsor last time out and should go well again in this one.

Genuine Article has only won one race and that was his 2nd run back in July 2023 in a maiden over a mile at Killarney. He has run thirteen times since without success but his 3rd place last week was only his second run since last September and he should have every chance dropped to his lowest ever mark of 80 in first time cheek pieces.

A slight drop in class could give & ½ a furlong more could be just what the doctor ordered for Ross O'Sullivan's 5 year old German Gelding QUAR SHAMAR who 'Should/Could' be better now after his run 34 days ago at the Curragh where he was only 3½ furlongs off the winner keeping on after a 258 day sabbatical. Trainer Ross O'Sullivan has a respectable 28.57% win strike rate this past year here at Galway & you would find yourself in profit had you backed blindly each way every time trainer has hired Rider Donagh 'O Connor this past year (26.67% place strike rate). Look if we get a glimmer of the charge that finished just 4 lengths off Paddington in the 2023 Irish 2,000 Guineas then you would be foolish to totally write this German lad off BUT then again it's the Galway Festival so what do I know? Each way at 18/1 with 5 places is enough for me.

This is mighty tough to break down with some of these which just met two days ago. One that caught the eye was Titanium. Always last, it made good headway but ran wide before finishing best of all under Nicola Burns. It gets a better draw today and a 7 lb claimer up in Gettigan, and the extra furlong looks sure to suit.

When i was looking earlier this morning the going was good and there were a couple i liked for win purposes and a couple for ew. I now see the going is soft which changes everything, even my ew tip. Considered Pink Oxalis who won for me lto, but is up 9lb and has an awful draw, but unfortunatly so does my pick Earls which is why i've gone win only. (still ew for betting) Was top weight lto (Saturday) and ran ok for 5th, but jockey did nothing in the straight and was given a very easy ride which now looks like a prep run for this race. Will need some luck with this draw but seems to prefer softer going nowadays and can only think this 16-1 price is because of the draw.

Strong run when second to Masoun at Leopardstown (nine furlongs) on penultimate start. Likely still capable just 2 pounds higher than for that run. Chris Hayes rides for William Durkan (SR 20%). Decent draw in stall 3.

2nd reserve SHIGAR might be easy to overlook, but digging a little deeper reveals a few interesting details. He ran very well here last year, finishing 4th of 17, beaten by 4.5 lengths off 82. He’s had 3 runs this term and hasn’t shown much, so it is risky. But the handicapper has given him a chance, down to 75 from a season opening 84. He’s 5lb below his last winning mark and a 2x distance winner. From a low draw and with a 10lb claimer, this might be an opportunity to show improvement.

WHICH WOLF WINS has been placed in one race from four starts. Second over 6f at Curragh on his latest outing earlier this month. Upped in trip to 7f should suit and could well be able to win this race.
